country: Not reported (single university hospital; European journal)
models_evaluated: commercial AI software for intracranial hemorrhage detection (unnamed)

links.outcome: Prospective silent-mode AI performance versus radiology residents on live emergency CT
links.effect: AI sensitivity 84% and specificity 94.4% vs residents 96.4% and 99.6% (p<0.001); AI did not outperform residents, so silent-mode prospective evaluation exposed underperformance before clinical use.
links.quote: Results from the AI software were stored in a separate PACS partition and were unavailable to the radiologists for the case reading.

links.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with on-call radiology residents on the same CT scans
links.effect: AI sensitivity 84% and specificity 94.4% vs residents 96.4% and 99.6% (p-values < 0.001); AI did not offer superior performance.
links.quote: Radiology residents demonstrated a significantly higher performance in detecting ICH compared to the AI software.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of a commercial AI diagnostic tool deployed in parallel (silent mode) on consecutive emergency department CT scans to compare its diagnostic performance against radiology residents.
